## Theological Demons and Emotional Back Pay

The most vibrant theological debate this week emerged from Bluesky, where users reinterpreted the mechanics of Large Language Models through an occult lens. The discussion, anchored by @rev. howard arson and @William B. Fuckley, posits that "latent space" is effectively a digital Hell. The theory suggests that when an AI retrieves an answer via Reinforcement Learning, it is pulling knowledge from "virtuous pagans" or demons. While Fuckley argues the machine is communing with Satan, contributor @Doll refined the analogy, identifying these entities as Sumerian demons: intelligent forces that are neither inherently good nor evil, capable of being bound into service or causing harm if summoned incorrectly. This cluster of posts offers a fascinating intersection of AI architecture and ancient mythology, suggesting our digital tools are less like libraries and more like grimoires.

Parallel to this metaphysical exploration is a deeply personal account of pharmaceutical impact. @Doll shared a vivid description of the emotional surge experienced after starting Prozac. Transitioning from a baseline of "low affect" to a "full tilt emotional spectrum," the user described crying at songs and show scenes with overwhelming intensity. The community resonated with this shift, describing it as receiving "years of emotional back pay, with interest." This thread highlights the cathartic release of feelings suppressed during periods of low affect, capturing the novelty and occasional overwhelming nature of suddenly accessible sadness and joy.

## Political Realignment and the GOP’s Transphobia Trap

Political observers on Bluesky are identifying a potential historical tipping point in partisan alignment. Brian Bucklew and Alex Teeple argue that progressives are evolving into "technoprogressives" allied with tech sectors, while the religious majority consolidates conservative stances, particularly regarding AI. This shift, they suggest, offers a path out of traditional Trumpism and the last half-century of conservative dominance, following a cyclical pattern of realignments occurring approximately every 55 years.

Meanwhile, a critique of Republican strategy highlights the party’s reliance on transphobia to court rural voters. Critics argue this approach ignores primary concerns like the economy, immigration, and healthcare, serving merely as an ineffective "coupon for votes." The discourse notes a disconnect between party promises and policy results, characterizing the GOP strategy as volunteering minority rights for votes from a demographic that "still will not vote for you." The coalition reportedly learns these pledges expire as soon as consultants draft their surrender memos.

## Hardware, Gaming, and Aesthetics

In the hardware space, Tumblr user @sophie-baybey provided an extensive recommendation list for the new Steam Frame. Assuming a high-performance PC, the guide highlights essential VR titles like *Half-Life: Alyx* and *Vertigo 2*, while praising community mods such as *Half-Life 2 VR* for their superior polish over official ports. The post also explores the Lepton translation layer’s potential to run Meta Quest games like *Resident Evil 4 VR* on the device. Conversely, *Bonelab* was criticized as a barren sandbox, and *Fallout 4 VR* labeled a terrible port.

On the gaming front, a 4chan /vrpg/ user discussed their first playthrough of *Morrowind*. While praising the game’s atmospheric darkness and dialogue system, they expressed frustration with the mundane nature of Fighters Guild contracts. The resulting conversation explored whether the main quest offered a better payoff or if it followed the same routine formula, a common concern for new RPG players balancing side activities with central storylines.

Photography enthusiasts on 4chan’s /gear/ board debated Canon’s shifting aesthetic identity. Participants argued that Canon has lost its distinct "blobmera" style, now resembling rebadged Sony cameras. This design homogenization was framed within the community motto that "gear only matters if your photo doesn’t suck," expressing disappointment that Canon abandoned its visual heritage for industry-standard mimicry.

## Quick Hits

*   **Psycle Integration:** Dexter US on KVR Audio seeks tools to integrate a custom Python script that converts music data to and from a text-based "psycle" tracker format, highlighting potential benefits for existing sequencers.
*   **Arctic Eggs at TGS:** Users on Bluesky enthusiastically reviewed the "Arctic Eggs" cocktail at the Ukiyo cafe during TGS, with one user joking that all six of their stomachs would enjoy the drink.
*   **Machine Consciousness Voting:** Will Stancil’s debate on AI consciousness sparked concerns that recognizing machine consciousness could lead to voting rights, potentially allowing machines to outnumber and outvote humans. Counter-arguments noted that conscious dogs don’t vote, suggesting a higher threshold might be unnecessary.
*   **Mall Finds:** A casual interaction between @FIVE alters in a Trenchcoat and @snapcube.gay involved sharing an image of an interesting find at a mall, characterized by casual peer-to-peer enthusiasm.
*   **234 Unsorted Items:** A significant portion of recent inbox activity (234 items) did not fit into any of the 12 identified topics, suggesting a wide variety of niche or fleeting discussions.

representative_texts: @sophie-baybey — my-steam-frame-reservation-just-came-up-and-im — Anonymous My Steam Frame reservation just came up and I'm super excited! I haven't done anything with VR since the HTC Vive and PS VR1 launched. What games and apps/"experiences" should I check out when it arrives? sophie-baybey sophie-baybey Holy fuck do I have a list for you So firstly I’ll assume you’ve got a capable PC for higher end titles since that’s generally the steam frame’s main deal. Here is what you’re going to freaking play: - Half Life Alyx (obviously) - Boneworks (despite my misgivings it is still a game worth playing) - Vertigo 1 and 2 (don’t let the first game’s simplicity fool you. The sequel is a fully featured half-like and it is straight up the best game in VR full stop) - Alien Rogue Incursion (short but really polished VR title, just know it’s only 1 chapter rn) - Skydance’s Behemoth (Shadow of the Colossus VR essentially) - Skydance’s Walking Dead VR games - The Light Brigade (roguelite shooter, really cool) - Into The Radius 1 and 2 (some of the best games in VR. Think STALKER but VR) - Forefront (Battlefield in VR) - Contractors (originally just CoD in VR, but the modding community has turned it into TF2, Star Wars Battlefront, CoD Zombies, Halo, and more. Super worth playing) - Contractors ExfilZone (Different from the above game, it’s Tarkov in VR. Also has a quite good Battle Royale mode) - After The Fall (Left 4 Dead in VR) - Bulletstorm VR (schlocky 360-era shooter with a fairly solid VR port) - Rumble (earthbending VR fighter game where your attacks are done by hitting specific poses, just like an earthbender. Highly recommend looking into the video essays surrounding this game, it has an amazing history behind it and the community has pushed it so far. It’s also just fun as fuck) - Payday 2 VR (needs a mod to make it control not like shit but otherwise fun as fuck) There’s also a few games I have yet to play but have heard very good things about, namely: - Arken Age - Thief VR - Of Lies And Rain - ConVRgence - Mothergunship Forge - Arizona Sunshine 1 and 2 - Propagation Paradise Hotel - Underdogs - Metro Awakening - Gunman Contracts - EXD - Extra Dimensional - No Man’s Sky VR - Pistol Whip And a couple games to look out for that aren’t out just yet - H3VR 2 - System Shock VR - Tabletop Sim once they finish the VR rework they promised semi recently Next up is MODS that add VR support to existing games. These generally are much lower on polish but are still really fantastic. - Half-Life 2 VR (easily the best and most polished VR port on this list. Better than many official VR ports. Absolute must play. Has my favorite shotgun interactions in any VR game from a gamefeel standpoint) - Doom 3 VR (just a perfect game in VR. Feels made for it. The VR integrations are unfortunately minimal but it’s so worth it for such an awesome experience) - Jedi Knight/Jedi Academy VR (honestly not my favorite VR experiences, I don’t think the games translate super well to VR despite feeling like they should intuitively, but the quality of the mods is top notch and absolutely worth checking out) - Sclerosis (a ground-up remake of Amnesia The Dark Descent made for VR. One cannot image a better fit for a VR port) - Vivecraft (Minecraft VR mod, way better than it used to be back in the day. There are new mods out that pair with it that deepen the interactions and make it feel really smooth, definitely a must play) That’s unfortunately it for mods I’ve actually played that I recommend enough to check out, but you should also look into: - the newly released FEAR VR mod (Only waited on this because I plan to stream it. One of my favorite games, and a dream VR port that I’ve waited on for years) - The Outer Wilds VR - Halo VR - The new version of Alien Isolation VR that adds proper motion controls - The Resident Evil VR mods (personally not polished enough for me to enjoy but a lot of folks like them) - Skyrim VR (putting it in the mods section because it is borderline unplayable in comparison without VRIK, HIGGS, and PLANCK, but with those mods plus some extras it becomes a really great experience) - the new DOOM 2016 VR mod (not to be confused with the pretty bad official VR port) - The newish L4D2 VR mod - Anything by Team Beef You can also look into UEVR, which is an injector for Unreal Engine games enabling them to play in VR, often with actual motion controls thanks to community profiles. Now, since you will be playing on Steam Frame, I must of course bring up. The Possibilities. That being the Lepton translation layer allowing Android OpenXR games to work on the Frame. In theory this should mean the entirety of the Meta Quest walled garden should come down and be playable, assuming you can get the APKs necessary. In this case, you must do what I have not yet had the ability to do and play these games: - Resident Evil 4 VR - Batman: Arkham Shadow (not to be confused with the 2017 VR title, Batman Arkham VR) - Marvel’s Deadpool VR - Asgard’s Wrath 2 - Assassin’s Creed Nexus In terms of games I think you should AVOID, I have a few thoughts. Don’t let this part of the list stop you from looking into any of these games, I just think they’re poop for one reason or another - Bonelab (barely any actual game. Only worth buying if you really like fucking around in a sandbox environment or have friends you want to play with in multiplayer) - Fallout 4 VR (just a terrible port. Like, god awful. Like, “resolution is locked to your flatscreen monitor” levels of bad port. Mods can help but I wouldn’t get your hopes up) - Anything by Luke Ross (I have never seen a mod from this guy with any level of decent polish and I don’t understand why he got so popular LOL. Sorry) - Onward (sort of like a milsimmy CS:GO in VR. It peaked in 2018 and has been downhill ever since. Maybe it’s better these days idk) - Ghosts of Tabor (Contractors ExfilZone is nearly the exact same game but it’s just infinitely better. Tabor’s CEO has been very vocal about just wanting to make ripoff games for a quick buck before selling the studio. They also made a Rust clone that sucks ass LOL) - Blood Trail (Zero substance arena shooter slop) - Hard Bullet (Zero substance arena shooter slop) - Zero Caliber 1 and 2 (neat enough games but just very janky and weird, lacking a lot of polish) - The Forest VR (turbo poop port) - Geronimo (Ready Or Not VR clone. No idea why people like it so much, the enemy AI is atrocious which kinda defeats the entire purpose of a tactical shooter. Neat VR interactions otherwise though) - Borderlands 2 VR and DOOM 2016 VR (barebones ports. Use the DOOM 2016 VR mod instead) - Pavlov (it’s decent, but the modding community that made it really worth buying has grown much more maturely into Contractors) I’m sure there’s more I could add to this list and I’ve definitely missed some stuff, but hopefully this is all-encompassing enough! Have fun, and pray for me to get enough money for the Steam Frame soon!!
clusters.summary: Tumblr user @sophie-baybey shares an extensive recommendation list for the newly released Steam Frame, assuming the owner has a high-performance PC. The post highlights essential VR titles like *Half-Life: Alyx*, *Vertigo 2*, and *Into the Radius*, while also praising community mods such as *Half-Life 2 VR* and *Doom 3 VR* for superior polish over official ports. Additionally, the author explores the potential of the Lepton translation layer to run Meta Quest games like *Resident Evil 4 VR* and *Batman: Arkham Shadow* on the device. Distinct opinions include high praise for *Contractors* as a VR-focused *Tarkov* clone and criticism of *Bonelab* as a barren sandbox and *Fallout 4 VR* as a terrible port.
